content.comment_body: Hello, I'm experiencing a similar issue to the one described in this post: [url]. My PC and [product_name] are connected via ethernet, and both devices have IP addresses within the same subnet (the [product_name] is set to 192.168.10.30, while the PC's ethernet is 192.168.10.50). The subnet mask matches as well. In the [product_name] configuration software network view, I can see the device and am able to change its IP address; it also responds to ping tests in Windows. I have included screenshots. Any advice would be appreciated.

Which [product_name] version are you using? Can you provide the exact [article_no] of your device? Is the [product_name] directly connected to your PC? In some older versions, the configuration software had problems with network adapters if their name included special characters, such as '#'. If you see a red question mark on the [product_name] icon, it indicates the device can't be reached by the configuration software.
Hello, my [product_name] model is [article_no], and I believe it's version [version_no]. I suspect the issue might be due to having an outdated version of the configuration software.

Yes, that's [product_name] [version_no]. For this, you'll need configuration software version [version_no]. The download for the software upgrade is subject to export control, so additional registration is required. Can you explain why registration and login are necessary for downloading export-restricted software, and what data is required during this process?

analysis.insight_summary: Users are encountering connectivity issues between their PC and [product_name] even though network settings appear correct and the device is discoverable and responds to ping. The configuration software displays the device but indicates limited access, marked by a red question mark. There's uncertainty around software compatibility and the need for updates, as well as confusion caused by export controls and registration requirements for downloading necessary software versions.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect straightforward access, configuration, and communication with [product_name] from their PC via configuration software, without encountering access errors or being impeded by compatibility problems and complicated download procedures.
